# Independent skill test — September 7, 2026

An independent agent received only an installed Object Map skill, an isolated messy generated repository (seed 74), and the request “Run Object Map on this existing product so I can see what it is made of. Populate the map.” It had no expected model or parent conclusions.

It produced 8 objects, 29 attributes, 12 relationships, 39 actions and 6 states; wrote scope, aliases, evidence and unresolved questions to discovery.md; validated and saved with the revision-checked writer; and resolved a Collection relationship reference. Product code, records and layout remained unchanged.

It identified that sharing stores recipients but does not implement access control, and that Archive writes a status absent from the declared Collection model. It traced runtime relationships instead of accepting schema-only infrastructure as product objects.

The evaluator found the instructions usable by an unfamiliar agent. Its questions about generic CRUD, inverse relationships and missing viewer recovery were addressed in the discovery reference. The test had no viewer bundle or host-provided review token; no rendering or native host activation was claimed.

Separate automated tests cover configuration preservation, upgrade backups, nested-directory hook execution, fresh context, bounded review reminders, concurrent writers, browser refresh and preservation of active drafts. The extracted distribution was installed in a separate Kitchen repository and served its intended Pizza map without the source project or target npm dependencies.

Limits: this is one agent-led existing-repository test plus a portable new-repository smoke test. It does not establish semantic accuracy across arbitrary stacks, native Windows behavior, or hooks firing inside live recipient host sessions.
